verdicts.why: Names the people present by metonymy without any attitude toward them.
A plain classifying term for a set of related things, as in 'family of languages'.
Technical taxonomic rank; purely descriptive.
States kinship; any warmth comes from the relationship itself, not from the word chosen over 'kin' or 'relative'.
Calling a non-kin group a 'family' (the company family) is a warm, affectionate framing that claims closeness and loyalty beyond what 'organization' or 'association' says.
The dignity of 'city fathers' is in the sense's meaning (distinguished position) rather than an added attitude of the speaker.
Names a role in a crime organization; the unpleasant referent does not make the word itself take a side.
Plain verb for hoping on someone's behalf, as in 'wish you luck'.
Neutral verb of invoking something upon someone, good or bad.
The everyday neutral verb for putting a question.
Neutral verb for requesting and expecting something, alongside 'require' and 'expect'.
Plain commercial sense of naming a price; no attitude toward the seller or buyer.
Neutral verb for inviting someone out or over.
Plain verb for getting together; no judgement of the parties.
Neutral verb for satisfying a requirement or need.
Neutral verb for encountering a reaction, as in 'met with opposition'.
Geometric or spatial description of things coming together.
Plain description of physical contact.
Neutral verb for assembling in one place.
Neutral sporting or military sense of facing an opponent.
Neutral verb for undergoing a fate; the bad referent in 'met his death' is not in the word.
A figurative but non-judging term for an earliest period.
The plain verb for starting something.
'Doesn't begin to' intensifies how far short something falls; that is strong meaning rather than an attitude added on top of it.
The plain verb for having a beginning.
